Rashi on Pesachim 87a:10:1.hebrew: שאוגדות פתחיהן לבעליהן - סותמות פתחיהן עד שמזדקקות לבעליהן, ואינן נבעלות לאחרים. לשון אחר: שמגידות פתחיהן של נדה לבעליהן לפרוש מהן, ואע"פ שתאוותן רבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:10:1.english: Who bind their openings for their husbands - They seal their openings until they are united with their husbands, and they do not have relations with others. Another interpretation: that they report their openings of menstruation [i.e., the onset of their flow] to their husbands, to separate from them, even though their desire is great.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:10:2.hebrew: וכן הוא אומר ומלאו כמזרק כזויות מזבח - מה זויות דהתם כתיב בהו ומלאו, הכא נמי בנותינו כזויות — על ידי שמתמלאות תאוה ואין נזקקות אלא עד שיבואו בעליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:10:2.english: And similarly it states: "And they shall be filled like the basins, like the corners of the altar" - Just as regarding the corners there, it is written "and they shall be filled," so too here, "our daughters as corners" [is] because they become filled with desire, yet do not engage [in relations] until their husbands come.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:11:1.hebrew: כאילו נבנה היכל בימיהן - דהכי משמע: מחוטבות בבנין היכל. תבנית — לשון בנין:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:11:1.english: As though the Sanctuary were built in their days - For this is what [the verse] means: carved in the building of the Sanctuary; "tavnit" [is] an expression of building.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:12:1.hebrew: בימי עוזיהו כו' - משום דאיירי בכנסת ישראל בלשון אשה הנשאת לבעל, כדאמרן "כמוצאת שלום", נקט נמי להא דהושע, דכתיב ביה "תקראי אישי", כדדריש לקמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:12:1.english: In the days of Uzziah, etc. - Because [the Gemara] was speaking of the Congregation of Israel in terms of a woman married to a husband, as we said [earlier], "as one that found peace," [it] also cited this [passage] from Hosea, in which it is written, "You shall call Me 'my husband,'" as [it] expounds below.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:12:2.hebrew: ארבעה נביאים - לקמיה מפרש להו, ובכולהו כתב בהו ״בימי עוזיהו יותם אחז יחזקיה״, שכולן החלו להינבא בימי עוזיהו וקיפחו חיי ארבעה מלכים:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:12:2.english: Four prophets - Further on, [the Gemara] explains [who] they [are], and regarding all of them it is written: “in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, [and] Hezekiah,” for all of them began to prophesy in the days of Uzziah and outlived four kings.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:13:1.hebrew: לא דיו שלא אמר כן - אתה למד ממה שאמר לו הקדוש ברוך הוא "קח לך אשת זנונים", ולא אמר כן לנביא אחר. (מצאתי כאן הגה"ה מלשון רבינו: ארבעה נביאים, כולהו כתיב בהו "בימי עוזיהו", בר ממיכה דכתיב ביה "יותם אחז יחזקיהו", ובעמוס לא כתיב אלא "עוזיהו". ומיהו מיכה בימיו נתנבא, אלא שכבר נתנגע, ויותם בנו שופט על הארץ, לפיכך לא נקרא על שמו. אבל שלשה היו קודם שנצטרע: בעמוס נאמר "שנתים לפני הרעש", וישעיה ביום הרעש, דכתיב (ישעיהו ו׳:ד׳) "וינועו אמות הספים" — שרעשו עליונים לשורפו ותחתונים לבולעו, כמשפט קרח ועדתו שערערו על הכהונה, ואותו היום נתנגע. והושע קודם לכולן.):
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:13:1.english: Not only did he fail to say that - You learn [this] from what the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: "Take for yourself a wife of harlotry," and He did not say so to any other prophet. (I found here a gloss from the language of our Master [Rashi]: [Of the] four prophets, in all of them is written "in the days of Uzziah," except for Micah, in which is written "Jotham, Ahaz, [and] Hezekiah"; and in Amos only "Uzziah" is written. However, Micah [also] prophesied in his days, except that [Uzziah] had already been stricken with leprosy, and Jotham his son was judging the land; therefore it was not called by [Uzziah's] name. But the [other] three were before he became leprous: in Amos it is stated, "two years before the earthquake"; and Isaiah [was] on the day of the earthquake, as it is written (Isaiah 6:4): "And the posts of the door moved" — for the upper [realms] quaked to burn him and the lower [realms] to swallow him, like the judgment of Korah and his congregation who challenged the priesthood, and on that very day he was stricken with leprosy. And Hosea preceded all of them.)

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:14:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן - אומר לו: קח לך אשת זנונים, ואחר כך אומר לו: שלחה:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:14:1.english: This is the reading - He says to him: "Take for yourself a wife of prostitution," and afterward He says to him: "Send her away."

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:14:2.hebrew: וילדי זנונים - שתלד לך בנים זנונים, ספק שלך, ספק של אחרים:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:14:2.english: And children of prostitution - That she will bear for you children of prostitution, [who are] possibly yours, possibly someone else's.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:14:3.english: [They] finish with her - [That is,] their intercourse and the desires of their heart.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:1:1.hebrew: האשה. תאכל משל בעלה - דמסתמא דעתה לימנות על של בעלה, כל זמן שלא פירשה שיהא דעתה בשל אביה:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:1:1.english: A woman. She shall eat from her husband's - For presumably her intention is to be registered on her husband's [Paschal lamb], as long as she did not specify that her intention is on her father's.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:1:2.english: The first Festival - Such is the custom of married women, to go to their father's house [on] the first Festival after the marriage.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:1:3.hebrew: תאכל ממקום שהיא רוצה - ובגמרא מוקי לה כשאינה רדופה לילך עד הנה לבית אביה תמיד. הלכך, מספקא לן בהי ניחא לה, אלא אם כן פירשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:1:3.english: She may eat from the place she wishes - And in the Gemara, [it] establishes [this case] as when she is not accustomed to always go to her father's house until now. Therefore, we are in doubt as to which one she prefers, unless she specified [beforehand].

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:2:1.english: Guardians - [Where] he had two [guardians], and this one registered him for his Paschal lamb and that one [registered him] for his Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:2:2.hebrew: לא יאכל משל שניהן - לא מפסחו של זה ולא משל זה. ואפילו המנהו האחד על פסחו, מי נתן רשות לחלק האחר לימנות על זה? ואין לו תקנה אלא א"כ רצו שניהן שימנה עם האחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:2:2.english: He may not eat from [that] of either of them - Neither from the Paschal lamb of this [master] nor from [that] of that [master]. And even if one [of them] registered him for his Paschal lamb, who gave permission to the other part [of him] to be registered for this [lamb]? And he has no remedy unless both of them consented that he be registered with one [of them].

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:2:3.english: He may not eat from his master's [lamb] - For presumably his master did not intend for the free portion [of him] to be registered on his Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:3:1.hebrew: שמעת מינה יש ברירה - קס"ד ממקום שהיא רוצה בשעת אכילה קאמר, ואמרינן הוברר דשחיטה וזריקה דהאי פסח שפיר איזדריק עלה דהאי אתתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:3:1.english: You learn from it [that] there is retroactive clarification - We initially assumed [that the Mishnah] is saying from whichever place she wishes at the time of eating, and we say [that] it is retroactively clarified that the slaughter and sprinkling of this Paschal lamb were properly sprinkled for this woman.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:3:2.english: At the time of slaughter - That we asked her at the time of slaughter, and she said, "I want this one."

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:4:1.english: She eats from her father’s [Paschal lamb] - As a matter of course.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:5:1.hebrew: מתניתין בשאינה רדופה - לילך תמיד לבית אביה, דבית בעלה חביב לה, הלכך כל שאר הרגלים ודאי שייכא בתריה, ורגל ראשון ספק. וברייתא ברדופה, הלכך רגל הראשון ודאי בתר אביה, מכאן ואילך ספק:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:5:1.english: The Mishnah [refers] to one who is not eager - to go constantly to her father's house, for her husband's house is dear to her; therefore, [on] all the other festivals she is certainly attached to him, and [on] the first festival [it is] uncertain. And the Baraita [refers] to one who is eager; therefore, [on] the first festival [she is] certainly [attached] to her father, [and] from then on [it is] uncertain.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:6:1.english: As one who finds peace - I became beloved to Him and was found whole to Him.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:6:2.english: To tell her praise - How accepted she is in her father-in-law's house.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:7:2.english: She has no [breasts] - For there is no benefit [derived] from her.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:7:3.hebrew: זו עילם - שהיה בה דניאל, שנאמר (דניאל ח׳:ב׳): ואני (דניאל הייתי) בשושן אשר בעילם המדינה, וזכה ללמוד ולא רבץ תורה בישראל. אבל בבל גידלה עזרא הסופר, דכתיב (עזרא ז׳:י׳): (הוא) הכין לבבו לדרוש (בתורת) [את תורת] ה' [ולעשות] וללמד בישראל חק ומשפט:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:7:3.english: This is Elam - For Daniel was in it, as it is stated (Daniel 8:2): "And I [Daniel, was] in Shushan, which is in the province of Elam," and he merited to learn, yet he did not disseminate Torah in Israel. However, Babylonia raised Ezra the Scribe, as it is written (Ezra 7:10): "[He] had set his heart to study the Torah of the Lord, and to do [it], and to teach in Israel statute and judgment."

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:8:1.hebrew: ושדי אלו ת"ח - המניקין אחרים כשדיים הללו:
Rashi on Pesachim 87a:8:1.english: And my breasts; these are the Torah scholars - Who nurse others [with Torah] like these breasts.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:8:2.english: Like towers - For they protect the generation.

Rashi on Pesachim 87a:9:1.english: As plants - Young saplings that have not yet been spoiled and have suffered no breakage.

Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:10:1.hebrew: כזויות מזבח - מה להלן דם, אף כאן דם נדות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:10:1.english: "Like the corners of the altar" - Just as there [there is] blood, so too here [there is] menstrual blood.

Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:12:1.hebrew: בימי עוזיהו - נתנבאו ד' נביאים. אע"ג דבמיכה לא כתיב ביה עוזיהו אלא "בימי יותם אחז יחזקיהו", מ"מ כיון דכתיב קרא סתם, י"ל שבתחלת מלכות יותם נתנבא, ואז היה עדיין עוזיהו חי, אלא שנתנגע ומלך יותם בנו תחתיו בימיו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:12:1.english: "In the days of Uzziah" - Four prophets prophesied [in his days]. Even though in [the Book of] Micah, Uzziah is not written, only "in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah," nevertheless, since the verse is written without specification, one can say that he prophesied at the beginning of Jotham's reign, and at that time Uzziah was still alive, except that he had been stricken with leprosy and his son Jotham reigned in his stead during his lifetime.

Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:14:1.hebrew: אמר לו הקב"ה להושע - ממה שאמר לו לקחת אשת זנונים, דריש שמסתמא כך אמר לו וכך השיבו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:14:1.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Hosea - From [the fact] that He told him to take a wife of prostitution, [the Gemara] expounds that presumably this is what He said to him and this is how he answered Him:

Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:1:1.hebrew: האשה. מאי רוצה בשעת שחיטה - ודווקא ביררה בשעת שחיטה, אבל לא ביררה — אינה אוכלת לא משל זה ולא משל זה; אבל ברישא, אפילו סתמא אוכלת משל בעלה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:1:1.english: HaIshah. "What is [the meaning of] 'she wishes'? At the time of slaughter" - And [this applies] specifically [where] she made her choice at the time of slaughter, but [if] she did not make her choice, she may not eat from either this one's or that one's; whereas in the first clause [of the Mishnah], even without specification, she eats from her husband's:

Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:5:1.hebrew: כאן ברדופה כאן בשאינה רדופה - אור"ת, דכל נשים רדופות הן להגיד בבית אביהן כשנמצאו שלימות בבית חמיהן. והשתא מוקי מתני' בשאינה רדופה, כגון שברגל הראשון שאחר חופה לא הלכה לבית אביה, ומיירי מתני' ברגל שני לחופתה והוא ראשון להליכה, שברגל שלפניו לא הלכה; הלכך, כיון שאינה רדופה, ספק הוא, דשמא גם בזה לא תלך, וצריכה לברר. אי נמי: מתניתין מיירי ברגל ראשון לחופתה, ואינה רדופה לפי שמיירי שכבר קודם הרגל הגידה שבחה בבית אביה, ולכך הוי ספק אף ברגל ראשון; ורישא דקתני "תאכל משל בעלה" — ברגל שני להליכתה, שכבר היתה בבית אביה ברגל שלפניו. וברייתא — ברדופה ברגל הראשון לחופתה ולהליכתה, דודאי דעתה בשל אביה, דהיא רדופה להגיד שבחה שנמצאת שלימה; ו"מכאן ואילך" דקתני, היינו ברגל שני ועדיין לא הגידה שבחה, דאז הוא ספק. ו"הלכה" דקתני במתניתין לאו דוקא, דאי דוקא — כבר גילתה דעתה שרוצה בשל אביה; א"נ, אפילו הלכה, כל זמן שלא ביררה ספק הוא. אבל "הלכה לעשות" לא גרס, ואי גרס — צ"ל ד"לעשות" לאו דווקא. והשתא אתי שפיר הא דגרס "דכתיב אז הייתי בעיניו כמוצאת שלום" וגו', וגרס נמי "וא"ר יוחנן", דמייתי ראיה דסתם כלה רדופה להגיד שבחה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 87a:5:1.english: Here [it is speaking] of [a woman who is] eager, [and] here of [one who is] not eager - Rabbeinu Tam says that all women are eager to tell in their father's house when they have been found whole in their father-in-law's house. And now [the Gemara] establishes our Mishnah as referring to [a woman] who is not eager, such as where on the first Festival after [her] wedding she did not go to her father's house, and our Mishnah is speaking of the second Festival after her wedding, which is the first [Festival] of [her] going [to her father's house], since on the Festival before it she did not go; therefore, since she is not eager, it is uncertain [which offering she intends to eat], for perhaps on this [Festival] as well she will not go, and [therefore] she must clarify [her intent]. Alternatively: our Mishnah is speaking of the first Festival after her wedding, and she is not eager because it is speaking of a case where already before the Festival she told of her praise in her father's house, and therefore it is uncertain even on the first Festival; and the first clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches "she shall eat from her husband's [offering]," [is speaking] of the second Festival of her going, since she was already in her father's house on the Festival before it. And the baraita [is speaking] of [a woman] who is eager on the first Festival after her wedding and of her going, where her mind is certainly on her father's [offering], since she is eager to tell of her praise that she was found whole; and "from here on" that [the baraita] teaches, that is on the second Festival when she has not yet told of her praise, for then it is uncertain. And "she went" that is taught in our Mishnah is not literal, for if [it were] literal — she would already have revealed her intent that she wants [to eat] from her father's [offering]; alternatively, even if she went, as long as she has not clarified [her intent], it is uncertain. However, [he] does not read "she went to observe," and if one does read [it], one must say that "to observe" is not literal. And now that which [he] reads works out well: "As it is written: 'Then I was in his eyes as one who finds peace,' etc.," and [he] also reads "And Rabbi Yochanan said," for [the Gemara] brings a proof that an ordinary bride is eager to tell of her praise.
